cards.text: A psalm of David, for the choirmaster, and David is talking to the LORD about the king. And friend, this king isn't a little bit happy. He is EXULTING, arms up, the whole thing!

cards.question: The king is rejoicing big time. What is he rejoicing in?

cards.text: Turns out the king had a desire in his heart and a request on his lips. David tells the LORD how that went, and then the psalm pauses: Selah.

cards.question: True or false: the LORD held back what the king asked for.

cards.text: And the LORD welcomes the king with rich blessings. Then He places something on the king's head, and I promise you it's fancier than my chef's hat.

cards.question: What does the LORD place on the king's head?

cards.text: Pure GOLD, friend. I went for twenty-five cents in a closing-sale bin, and this man is wearing a gold crown. Now hear what the king actually asked the LORD for.

cards.question: The king asked the LORD for ___.

cards.text: He asked for life, and the LORD granted it: "length of days, forever and ever." I hit snooze for five extra minutes and feel guilty all morning, and this king walks away with FOREVER, plus splendor and majesty!

cards.question: The LORD grants the king blessings forever and cheers him with joy in His ___.

cards.text: That is a LOT of blessing for one king. Then David says what's underneath it all, and it starts with something the king does.

cards.question: Under all those blessings, what is the one thing the king does?
The king trusts in the LORD, and through the loving devotion of the Most High, he will not be ___.

cards.text: Then the psalm turns from gold crowns to enemies: "Your right hand will seize those who hate You." That's a faster mood change than a group chat right after somebody types, "We need to talk."
At the time of the appearing, the enemies are placed in a fiery furnace. In His wrath the LORD will engulf them, and the fire will consume them.

cards.question: True or false: the descendants of those enemies will live on among the sons of men.
True or false: the enemies plan harm, but the schemes they come up with won't succeed.
Picture a bow trained right on those enemies. What happens to them?

cards.text: Last line, and now the psalm says "we." "Be exalted, O LORD, in Your strength." Sparkle would already be humming along, LOUD.

cards.question: In the psalm's last line, what do the people say they will do?

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 19 quotes "Be exalted, O LORD, in Your strength.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card spends words defining Selah as a pause ('then the psalm pauses: Selah'). That explains a hard word on the card, and it states one reading of a word whose meaning the text doesn't give. The card can name Selah, and the dictionary pop-up can cover its meaning.

rule.text: Don't spend card words explaining a hard word. Hard words get a dictionary pop-up (definitions.md, made after the cards).

findings.problem: The card cites only Psalm 21:4, but it retells the pure gold crown from Psalm 21:3. The only 21:4 content is the setup line. The citation should start at 21:3.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The card quotes Psalm 21:6 almost word for word and blanks its last word ('cheers him with joy in His ___'). No story card sets up 21:6. The baker can only guess the wording among presence, palace and city, which is a guess at the next words of a line rather than meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The setup joke 'Sparkle would already be humming along, LOUD' points straight at singing. That gives away card 20's answer ('Sing and praise His power') and rules out the other two answers.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.
